guide.title: Reassessment & Trending
guide.lead: Patients change, and you only notice if you look again. Repeat the primary assessment and vital signs on a schedule and after every intervention, then compare. A falling pulse in a bleeding patient is not good news.

steps.title: Primary assessment again
steps.text: XABCDE first: problems show here before the numbers change.

steps.title: Vital signs
steps.text: Every 5 minutes if unstable, every 15 minutes if stable, and after every intervention.

steps.title: Did it work?
steps.text: Check each intervention: oxygen, splint, tourniquet, drugs.

sections.title: Trends that mean trouble
rows: Pulse suddenly falls in a tachycardic trauma patient
GCS down by 2 points or more

quiz.q: Chest pain patient, pain-free after nitroglycerin, stable vital signs. Reassess every:
quiz.explanation: Back to every 5 minutes if anything changes.

quiz.q: Trauma: HR 124 at first, now 88 with BP 82/50. This means:
First thing to recheck in a reassessment:
Why is trending better than one reading?
options: It shows the direction: improving or deteriorating

quiz.q: A narrowing pulse pressure in trauma suggests:
quiz.explanation: Diastolic rises before the systolic falls.

quiz.q: GCS drops from 14 to 11. This is:
quiz.explanation: A fall of 2 points or more matters.

quiz.q: Reassessment after giving oxygen should include:
options: Whether SpO₂ and work of breathing improved

quiz.q: On reassessment the patient is worse. First?

options: Time-stamped vital signs and responses to treatment
quiz.explanation: Shows the trend to the hospital.

flashcards.question: Reassessment frequency
flashcards.answer: Unstable: every 5 minutes. Stable: every 15 minutes. And after every intervention.

flashcards.question: Parts of a reassessment
flashcards.answer: Primary assessment, vital signs, interventions, pain, mental status, transport decision.

flashcards.question: Why trend?
flashcards.answer: One reading is a snapshot; the trend shows if the patient is improving, stable or deteriorating.

flashcards.question: Sudden drop in heart rate in a tachycardic trauma patient
flashcards.answer: Pre-arrest: compensation has failed. Not improvement.

flashcards.question: Documenting reassessment
flashcards.answer: Time-stamped vital signs, GCS/AVPU, responses to treatment, pain, new findings.

flashcards.question: Narrowing pulse pressure
flashcards.answer: Vasoconstriction in early (compensated) shock: precedes hypotension.

flashcards.question: Deterioration on reassessment
flashcards.answer: Back to XABCDE, escalate treatment, call ALS, pre-alert, reconsider destination.

critical.scenario: GI bleed: at first alert, BP 104/68, HR 108. Fifteen minutes into transport she only opens her eyes to a loud voice; BP 84/52, HR 124 and thready, pale and sweaty.
critical.question: Best next action?

options.t: Back to XABCDE, oxygen to target, IV fluids per protocol, pre-alert the hospital, ALS intercept, faster transport
Continue routinely: she responds to voice
Stop to get a full history

critical.explanation: She has moved from compensated to decompensated shock; the hospital can prepare blood.
critical.kpi: Recognition of decompensated shock on reassessment

critical.scenario: COPD exacerbation: at first BP 148/92, HR 102, RR 28, SpO₂ 86%. After 10 minutes of oxygen and sitting up: BP 136/84, HR 96, RR 24, SpO₂ 93%, still working but feels better.
critical.question: What does the trend show?

options.t: Improving: continue, titrate oxygen to 88–92% if he retains CO₂, reassess in 5–15 minutes

options.f: Every value is moving the right way.

critical.explanation: If SpO₂ plateaus or he tires, consider CPAP/NIV per protocol.

critical.scenario: A head-injured patient was GCS 14 at the scene. Ten minutes later he's GCS 11 and his right pupil is larger.
critical.question: What now?

options.t: Serious deterioration: airway and ventilation to target EtCO₂, pre-alert the trauma centre, ALS, faster transport

options.f: A fall of 3 points with a new pupil change is an emergency.

options.t: Sit him up and give fluids to raise his BP high
options.f: Avoid hypotension, but the priority is airway and transport.

critical.explanation: A GCS fall of 2 points or more, or a new unequal pupil, suggests rising intracranial pressure.
critical.kpi: Recognizes neurological deterioration through serial GCS and pupil checks
